To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distal nephrons of the rabbit and human kidney are similar with respect to the distribution of the apical sodium and calcium transport pathways and that the apical sodium entry pathways in these two species are regulated by the same factors.
the apical sodium entry pathways in the distal nephrons of rabbit and human are identical, whereas the apical sodium exit pathways are not.

the apical plasma membranes of the distal convoluted tubule and of the connecting segment contain a high density of Na-K-2Cl cotransporters, and that the apical membrane of the cortical collecting duct is rich in Na-K-ATPase, epithelial sodium channels, and thiazide-sensitive sodium chloride cotransporters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the major sodium and calcium transport pathways in the distal nephrons, with the elucidation of their functional regulation, and with the understanding of how they contribute to the control of renal sodium and water excretion and of renal calcium handling.

the identification of transport proteins in the mammalian distals nephron, with the understanding of their cellular and molecular function, and with the translation of these data into the clinical management of renal sodium and water handling.
the identification of the major transport proteins and their distribution pattern along the mammalian renal distal nephron.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distal nephrons in rabbit, rat, mouse, and human are very similar, but not identical.
sodium and calcium transport along the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting duct is species-specific.
the distal nephrons of rabbit and human are similar in their overall organization of sodium and calcium pathways, but that there are also important differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sodium transport proteins are expressed along the entire cortical distal nephrons, with a distinct distribution pattern in different species, and that their expression is regulated by various factors, including hormones, tubular luminal content, flow rate, and dietary salt intake.
, in the human kidney, the distal convoluted tubule is the major site of apical sodium entry and that the thick ascending limb is a major site of calcium reabsorption.

the rabbit is an appropriate model to investigate the regulation of sodium and calcium reabsorption along the distal tubule, but the human kidney should be considered for the study of the final steps of transepithelial sodium transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apical sodium transport pathways of the cortical collecting duct are species-specific.
the rabbit is the most suitable animal model for the human kidney, and that the rat kidney is a poor model for the human one.
sodium transport in the distal nephrons is highly complex and that a better understanding of its regulation is needed to fully appreciate the role of the distal tubule in sodium balance.
